questions.text: Let $A=\{-2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4\}$. Let R be a relation on A defined by $xRy$ if and only if $2x+y\le2$. Let $l$ be the number of elements in R. Let m and n be the minimum number of elements required to be added in R to make it reflexive and symmetric relations respectively. Then $l+m+n$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ $(\alpha<\beta)$ are the roots of the equation $\left(-2+\sqrt{3}\right)\left(\left|\sqrt{x}-3\right|\right)+\left(x-6\sqrt{x}\right)+\left(9-2\sqrt{3}\right)=0$, $x\ge0$, then $\sqrt{\dfrac{\beta}{\alpha}}+\sqrt{\alpha\beta}$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
Put $u=\left|\sqrt{x}-3\right|$. Since $x-6\sqrt{x}+9=u^2$, the equation is $u^2+(\sqrt3-2)u-2\sqrt3=0$, i.e. $(u-2)(u+\sqrt3)=0$.
So $u=2$: $\sqrt{x}=5$ or $1$, giving $x=25$ or $1$. Thus $\alpha=1$, $\beta=25$.
$\sqrt{\dfrac{\beta}{\alpha}}+\sqrt{\alpha\beta}=5+5=10$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: A building construction work can be completed by two masons A and B together in 22.5 days. Mason A alone can complete the construction work in 24 days less than mason B alone. Then mason A alone will complete the construction work in :
questions.sol:
Let A take $a$ days, so B takes $a+24$ days.
$\dfrac1a+\dfrac1{a+24}=\dfrac1{22.5}=\dfrac2{45} \Rightarrow 45(2a+24)=2a(a+24) \Rightarrow a^2-21a-540=0$.
$(a-36)(a+15)=0$, so $a=36$ days.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $S=\{z: 3\le|2z-3(1+i)|\le7\}$ be a set of complex numbers. Then $\displaystyle\min_{z\in S}\left|\left(z+\frac12(5+3i)\right)\right|$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
Dividing by 2: $\dfrac32\le\left|z-\dfrac32(1+i)\right|\le\dfrac72$, an annulus with centre $C\left(\dfrac32,\dfrac32\right)$.
We need the least distance from $P\left(-\dfrac52,-\dfrac32\right)$ to S. $CP=\sqrt{4^2+3^2}=5$, which is more than the outer radius $\dfrac72$.
Minimum $=5-\dfrac72=\dfrac32$.

questions.text:
Among the statements :
I : If $\begin{vmatrix}1&\cos\alpha&\cos\beta\\\cos\alpha&1&\cos\gamma\\\cos\beta&\cos\gamma&1\end{vmatrix}=\begin{vmatrix}0&\cos\alpha&\cos\beta\\\cos\alpha&0&\cos\gamma\\\cos\beta&\cos\gamma&0\end{vmatrix}$, then $\cos^2\alpha+\cos^2\beta+\cos^2\gamma=\dfrac32$, and
II : If $\begin{vmatrix}x^2+x&x+1&x-2\\2x^2+3x-1&3x&3x-3\\x^2+2x+3&2x-1&2x-1\end{vmatrix}=px+q$, then $p^2=196q^2$,
questions.sol:
I: write $a,b,c$ for the cosines. The left side is $1-a^2-b^2-c^2+2abc$ and the right side is $2abc$, so $a^2+b^2+c^2=1$, not $\dfrac32$. I is false.
II: at $x=0$ the determinant is $\begin{vmatrix}0&1&-2\\-1&0&-3\\3&-1&-1\end{vmatrix}=-12$, so $q=-12$. At $x=1$ it is $\begin{vmatrix}2&2&-1\\4&3&0\\6&1&1\end{vmatrix}=12$, so $p=24$.
$p^2=576\neq196q^2=28224$, so II is false. Both are false.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: The sum of all possible values of $n\in\mathbf{N}$, so that the coefficients of $x$, $x^2$ and $x^3$ in the expansion of $(1+x^2)^2(1+x)^n$, are in arithmetic progression is :
questions.sol:
$(1+x^2)^2=1+2x^2+x^4$. Coefficients: $x$: $n$; $x^2$: $\binom n2+2$; $x^3$: $\binom n3+2n$.
A.P. condition: $2\left(\binom n2+2\right)=n+\binom n3+2n$. Multiplying by 6 and simplifying: $n^3-9n^2+26n-24=0$.
$(n-2)(n-3)(n-4)=0$, so $n=2,3,4$ and the sum is $9$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let the mean and variance of 8 numbers $-10, -7, -1, x, y, 9, 2, 16$ be $\dfrac72$ and $\dfrac{293}{4}$, respectively. Then the mean of 4 numbers $x, y, x+y+1, |x-y|$ is :
questions.sol:
Sum $=28$, and the known numbers add to $9$, so $x+y=19$.
$\sum x_i^2=8\left(\dfrac{293}{4}+\dfrac{49}{4}\right)=684$, and the known squares add to $491$, so $x^2+y^2=193$.
Then $xy=84$, so $\{x,y\}=\{12,7\}$ and $|x-y|=5$.
Mean $=\dfrac{19+20+5}{4}=11$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: A rectangle is formed by the lines $x=0$, $y=0$, $x=3$ and $y=4$. Let the line L be perpendicular to $3x+y+6=0$ and divide the area of the rectangle into two equal parts. Then the distance of the point $\left(\dfrac12, -5\right)$ from the line L is equal to :
questions.sol:
A line halves the area of a rectangle when it passes through its centre $\left(\dfrac32,2\right)$.
Perpendicular to $3x+y+6=0$: slope $\dfrac13$, so L: $x-3y+c=0$ with $\dfrac32-6+c=0$, i.e. $2x-6y+9=0$.
Distance of $\left(\dfrac12,-5\right)$: $\dfrac{|1+30+9|}{\sqrt{40}}=\sqrt{40}=2\sqrt{10}$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let the domain of the function $f(x)=\log_3\log_5\log_7\left(9x-x^2-13\right)$ be the interval $(m, n)$. Let the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$ have eccentricity $\dfrac n3$ and the length of the latus rectum $\dfrac{8m}{3}$. Then $b^2-a^2$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
Need $\log_5\log_7(9x-x^2-13)>0$, i.e. $9x-x^2-13>7$, i.e. $x^2-9x+20<0$: $x\in(4,5)$. So $m=4$, $n=5$.
$e=\dfrac53 \Rightarrow \dfrac{b^2}{a^2}=\dfrac{16}{9}$. Latus rectum $\dfrac{2b^2}{a}=\dfrac{32}{3} \Rightarrow b^2=\dfrac{16a}{3}$.
So $\dfrac{16a}{3}=\dfrac{16a^2}{9}$, $a=3$, $b^2=16$, and $b^2-a^2=7$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Number of solutions of $\sqrt3\cos2\theta+8\cos\theta+3\sqrt3=0$, $\theta\in[-3\pi, 2\pi]$ is :
questions.sol:
With $\cos2\theta=2\cos^2\theta-1$: $2\sqrt3\cos^2\theta+8\cos\theta+2\sqrt3=0$, i.e. $\sqrt3c^2+4c+\sqrt3=0$.
$c=\dfrac{-4\pm2}{2\sqrt3}$, so $\cos\theta=-\dfrac1{\sqrt3}$ (the other root $-\sqrt3$ is impossible).
$\cos\theta=k$ with $-1<k<0$ has two solutions in each of $[-3\pi,-\pi]$ and $[-\pi,\pi]$, and one in $[\pi,2\pi]$. Total $=5$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let the line $y-x=1$ intersect the ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{2}+\dfrac{y^2}{1}=1$ at the points A and B. Then the angle made by the line segment AB at the center of the ellipse is :
questions.sol:
Substituting $y=x+1$: $\dfrac{x^2}{2}+x^2+2x+1=1 \Rightarrow x\left(\dfrac{3x}{2}+2\right)=0$. So $A(0,1)$ and $B\left(-\dfrac43,-\dfrac13\right)$.
OA is along the positive $y$-axis. OB makes an angle with the positive $y$-axis whose cosine is $\dfrac{-1/3}{\sqrt{17}/3}=-\dfrac1{\sqrt{17}}$.
The angle is $\pi-\tan^{-1}4=\pi-\left(\dfrac\pi2-\tan^{-1}\dfrac14\right)=\dfrac\pi2+\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac14\right)$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text:
Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ respectively be the maximum and the minimum values of the function $f(\theta)=4\left(\sin^4\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{2}-\theta\right)+\sin^4(11\pi+\theta)\right)-2\left(\sin^6\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{2}-\theta\right)+\sin^6(9\pi-\theta)\right)$, $\theta\in\mathbf{R}$.
Then $\alpha+2\beta$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$\sin\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{2}-\theta\right)=-\cos\theta$, $\sin(11\pi+\theta)=-\sin\theta$, $\sin\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{2}-\theta\right)=-\cos\theta$, $\sin(9\pi-\theta)=\sin\theta$.
With $p=\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta$: $\sin^4+\cos^4=1-2p$ and $\sin^6+\cos^6=1-3p$.
$f=4(1-2p)-2(1-3p)=2-2p$, and $0\le p\le\dfrac14$. So $\alpha=2$, $\beta=\dfrac32$, and $\alpha+2\beta=5$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: The vertices B and C of a triangle ABC lie on the line $\dfrac{x}{1}=\dfrac{1-y}{-2}=\dfrac{z-2}{3}$. The coordinates of A and B are $(1, 6, 3)$ and $(4, 9, \alpha)$ respectively and C is at a distance of 10 units from B. The area (in sq. units) of $\Delta ABC$ is :
questions.sol:
The line is $\dfrac x1=\dfrac{y-1}{2}=\dfrac{z-2}{3}$, through $P(0,1,2)$ with direction $\vec d=(1,2,3)$. (B lies on it with $\alpha=14$.)
Height = distance of A from the line: $\overrightarrow{PA}=(1,5,1)$, $\overrightarrow{PA}\times\vec d=(13,-2,-3)$, so the distance is $\dfrac{\sqrt{182}}{\sqrt{14}}=\sqrt{13}$.
Area $=\dfrac12\times BC\times\sqrt{13}=\dfrac12\times10\times\sqrt{13}=5\sqrt{13}$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text:
Let $\vec a=-\hat i+\hat j+2\hat k$, $\vec b=\hat i-\hat j-3\hat k$, $\vec c=\vec a\times\vec b$ and $\vec d=\vec c\times\vec a$.
Then $\left(\vec a-\vec b\right)\cdot\vec d$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$\vec d=(\vec a\times\vec b)\times\vec a=(\vec a\cdot\vec a)\vec b-(\vec a\cdot\vec b)\vec a$, with $\vec a\cdot\vec a=6$ and $\vec a\cdot\vec b=-8$.
$\vec d=6\vec b+8\vec a=(-2,2,-2)$.
$\vec a-\vec b=(-2,2,5)$, so $(\vec a-\vec b)\cdot\vec d=4+4-10=-2$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let the direction cosines of two lines satisfy the equations : $4l+m-n=0$ and $2mn+10nl+3lm=0$. Then the cosine of the acute angle between these lines is :
questions.sol:
Put $n=4l+m$: $2m(4l+m)+10l(4l+m)+3lm=0 \Rightarrow 40l^2+21lm+2m^2=0 \Rightarrow (8l+m)(5l+2m)=0$.
$m=-8l$: $n=-4l$, direction $(1,-8,-4)$, length 9. $m=-\dfrac52l$: direction $(2,-5,3)$, length $\sqrt{38}$.
$\cos\theta=\dfrac{2+40-12}{9\sqrt{38}}=\dfrac{10}{3\sqrt{38}}$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text:
Let $f(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{ax^2+2ax+3}{4x^2+4x-3}, & x\neq-\dfrac32, \dfrac12\\ b, & x=-\dfrac32, \dfrac12\end{cases}$
be continuous at $x=-\dfrac32$. If $fof(x)=\dfrac75$, then $x$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$4x^2+4x-3=(2x+3)(2x-1)$. For a finite limit at $x=-\dfrac32$ the numerator must vanish there: $\dfrac{9a}{4}-3a+3=0 \Rightarrow a=4$.
Then $f(x)=\dfrac{(2x+1)(2x+3)}{(2x+3)(2x-1)}=\dfrac{2x+1}{2x-1}$ (and $b=\dfrac12$).
$f(f(x))=\dfrac{6x+1}{2x+3}=\dfrac75 \Rightarrow 30x+5=14x+21 \Rightarrow x=1$. Check: $f(1)=3$, $f(3)=\dfrac75$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $f(x)=\displaystyle\int\frac{\left(2-x^2\right)\cdot e^x}{\left(\sqrt{1+x}\right)(1-x)^{3/2}}\,dx$. If $f(0)=0$, then $f\left(\dfrac12\right)$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
Let $g(x)=\sqrt{\dfrac{1+x}{1-x}}=\dfrac{1-x^2}{\sqrt{1+x}(1-x)^{3/2}}$. Then $g'(x)=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1+x}(1-x)^{3/2}}$.
So the integrand is $e^x\left(g+g'\right)$ and $f(x)=e^xg(x)+C$. $f(0)=1+C=0$ gives $C=-1$.
$f\left(\dfrac12\right)=\sqrt e\cdot\sqrt3-1=\sqrt{3e}-1$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: The value of the integral $\displaystyle\int_{\pi/24}^{5\pi/24}\frac{dx}{1+\sqrt[3]{\tan2x}}$ is :
questions.sol:
Replace $x$ by $\dfrac\pi{24}+\dfrac{5\pi}{24}-x=\dfrac\pi4-x$; then $\tan2x$ becomes $\cot2x$, and $I=\displaystyle\int\frac{\sqrt[3]{\tan2x}}{1+\sqrt[3]{\tan2x}}dx$.
Adding the two forms: $2I=\displaystyle\int_{\pi/24}^{5\pi/24}dx=\dfrac\pi6$.
$I=\dfrac\pi{12}$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text:
Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $x^4dy+\left(4x^3y+2\sin x\right)dx=0$, $x>0$, $y\left(\dfrac\pi2\right)=0$.
Then $\pi^4y\left(\dfrac\pi3\right)$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$x^4dy+4x^3y\,dx=d\left(x^4y\right)$, so $d\left(x^4y\right)=-2\sin x\,dx$ and $x^4y=2\cos x+C$.
$y\left(\dfrac\pi2\right)=0$ gives $C=0$.
$y\left(\dfrac\pi3\right)=\dfrac{2\cdot\frac12}{(\pi/3)^4}=\dfrac{81}{\pi^4}$, so $\pi^4y\left(\dfrac\pi3\right)=81$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $|A|=6$, where A is a $3\times3$ matrix. If $\left|\operatorname{adj}\left(3\operatorname{adj}\left(A^2\cdot\operatorname{adj}(2A)\right)\right)\right|=2^m\cdot3^n$, $m, n\in\mathbf{N}$, then $m+n$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
For a $3\times3$ matrix, $|\operatorname{adj}M|=|M|^2$ and $|kM|=k^3|M|$.
$|2A|=48$, $|\operatorname{adj}(2A)|=48^2$, $\left|A^2\operatorname{adj}(2A)\right|=36\cdot48^2=2^{10}3^4$.
$|\operatorname{adj}(\ldots)|=2^{20}3^8$; times $3^3$ for the factor 3: $2^{20}3^{11}$; the outer adj squares it: $2^{40}3^{22}$.
$m+n=40+22=62$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: The number of 4-letter words, with or without meaning, which can be formed using the letters PQRPQRSTUVP, is __________.
questions.sol:
Letters: P three times, Q and R twice each, S, T, U, V once each (7 different letters).
All different: $^7P_4=840$.
One pair and two others: $3\times\binom62\times\dfrac{4!}{2!}=540$.
Two pairs: $\binom32\times\dfrac{4!}{2!2!}=18$.
Three P and one other: $6\times4=24$.
Total $=840+540+18+24=1422$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: From the first 100 natural numbers, two numbers first a and then b are selected randomly without replacement. If the probability that $a-b\ge10$ is $\dfrac mn$, $\gcd(m, n)=1$, then $m+n$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
Ordered pairs $(a,b)$, $a\ne b$: $100\times99=9900$.
For $a-b=d$ ($10\le d\le99$) there are $100-d$ pairs, so the favourable count is $1+2+\ldots+90=4095$.
$\dfrac{4095}{9900}=\dfrac{91}{220}$, so $m+n=311$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text:
Let $f$ be a twice differentiable non-negative function such that $\left(f(x)\right)^2=25+\displaystyle\int_0^x\left(\left(f(t)\right)^2+\left(f'(t)\right)^2\right)dt$.
Then the mean of $f\left(\log_e(1)\right), f\left(\log_e(2)\right), \ldots\ldots, f\left(\log_e(625)\right)$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
Differentiating: $2ff'=f^2+f'^2$, i.e. $(f-f')^2=0$, so $f'=f$ and $f=Ce^x$.
At $x=0$: $f(0)^2=25$ and $f\ge0$, so $f(x)=5e^x$ and $f(\log_ek)=5k$.
Mean $=\dfrac{5(1+2+\ldots+625)}{625}=\dfrac{5\times626}{2}=1565$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let the area of the region bounded by the curve $y=\max\{\sin x, \cos x\}$, lines $x=0$, $x=\dfrac{3\pi}{2}$, and the $x$-axis be A. Then, $A+A^2$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
$y=\cos x$ on $\left[0,\dfrac\pi4\right]$, $\sin x$ on $\left[\dfrac\pi4,\dfrac{5\pi}4\right]$ and $\cos x$ on $\left[\dfrac{5\pi}4,\dfrac{3\pi}2\right]$.
Areas: $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$; $\displaystyle\int_{\pi/4}^{\pi}\sin x\,dx=1+\dfrac1{\sqrt2}$; $\displaystyle\int_\pi^{5\pi/4}|\sin x|dx=1-\dfrac1{\sqrt2}$; $\displaystyle\int_{5\pi/4}^{3\pi/2}|\cos x|dx=1-\dfrac1{\sqrt2}$.
$A=3$, so $A+A^2=12$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Four persons measure the length of a rod as 20.00 cm, 19.75 cm, 17.01 cm and 18.25 cm. The relative error in the measurement of average length of the rod is :
questions.sol:
Mean $=\dfrac{75.01}{4}=18.75$ cm (18.7525).
Absolute deviations: 1.25, 1.00, 1.74, 0.50; mean absolute error $\approx1.12$ cm.
Relative error $=\dfrac{1.12}{18.75}\approx0.06$.

questions.text: An object is projected with kinetic energy $K$ from a point $A$ at an angle $60^\circ$ with the horizontal. The ratio of the difference in kinetic energies at points $B$ and $C$ to that at point $A$ (see figure), in the absence of air friction is :
questions.sol:
At the top B only the horizontal velocity $u\cos60^\circ$ remains: $K_B=K\cos^260^\circ=\dfrac K4$.
C is at the level of A, so $K_C=K$.
$\dfrac{K_C-K_B}{K_A}=\dfrac{3K/4}{K}=3:4$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two small balls with masses $m$ and $2m$ are attached to both ends of a rigid rod of length $d$ and negligible mass. If angular momentum of this system is $L$ about an axis $(A)$ passing through its centre of mass and perpendicular to the rod then angular velocity of the system about $A$ is :
questions.sol:
The centre of mass is $\dfrac{2d}{3}$ from $m$ and $\dfrac d3$ from $2m$.
$I=m\left(\dfrac{2d}{3}\right)^2+2m\left(\dfrac d3\right)^2=\dfrac{2md^2}{3}$.
$\omega=\dfrac LI=\dfrac32\dfrac{L}{md^2}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.text: The moment of inertia of a square loop made of four uniform solid cylinders, each having radius $R$ and length $L$ $(R<L)$ about an axis passing through the mid points of opposite sides, is (Take the mass of the entire loop as $M$) :
questions.sol:
Each cylinder has mass $\dfrac M4$. The axis lies in the plane of the loop.
Two cylinders are cut by the axis at their centres, perpendicular to their length: each $\dfrac M4\left(\dfrac{R^2}{4}+\dfrac{L^2}{12}\right)$.
Two cylinders are parallel to the axis at distance $\dfrac L2$: each $\dfrac M4\left(\dfrac{R^2}{2}+\dfrac{L^2}{4}\right)$.
Total $=\dfrac M2\left(\dfrac{3R^2}{4}+\dfrac{L^2}{3}\right)=\dfrac38MR^2+\dfrac16ML^2$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.text: A small bob $A$ of mass $m$ is attached to a massless rigid rod of length 1 m pivoted at point $P$ and kept at an angle of $60^\circ$ with vertical as shown in figure. At distance of 1 m below point $P$, an identical bob $B$ is kept at rest on a smooth horizontal surface that extends to a circular track of radius $R$ as shown in figure. If bob $B$ just manages to complete the circular path of radius $R$ upto a point $Q$ after being hit elastically by bob $A$, then radius $R$ is __________m.
questions.sol:
A falls through $1-\cos60^\circ=0.5$ m, so it reaches B with $v^2=2g(0.5)=g$.
An elastic collision between equal masses passes this speed fully to B.
To just get over the top of the circle, $v^2=5gR$ at the bottom: $g=5gR$, so $R=\dfrac15$ m.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two blocks with masses 100 g and 200 g are attached to the ends of springs $A$ and $B$ as shown in figure. The energy stored in $A$ is $E$. The energy stored in $B$, when spring constants $k_A$, $k_B$ of $A$ and $B$, respectively satisfy the relation $4k_A=3k_B$, is :
questions.sol:
At equilibrium $kx=mg$, so the stored energy is $\dfrac12kx^2=\dfrac{(mg)^2}{2k}$.
$\dfrac{E_B}{E_A}=\left(\dfrac{m_B}{m_A}\right)^2\dfrac{k_A}{k_B}=4\times\dfrac34=3$.
$E_B=3E$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The strain-stress plot for materials $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ is shown in the figure. Which material has the largest Young's modulus ?
questions.sol:
Here strain is on the vertical axis and stress on the horizontal axis, so the slope is $\dfrac{\text{strain}}{\text{stress}}=\dfrac1Y$.
The largest Young's modulus has the smallest slope: material $C$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
In a perfectly inelastic collision, two spheres made of the same material with masses 15 kg and 25 kg, moving in opposite directions with speeds of 10 m/s and 30 m/s, respectively, strike each other and stick together. The rise in temperature (in $^\circ$C), if all the heat produced during the collision is retained by these spheres, is :
(specific heat of sphere material 31 cal/kg.$^\circ$C and 1 cal $=$ 4.2 J)
questions.sol:
Loss of kinetic energy $=\dfrac12\dfrac{m_1m_2}{m_1+m_2}v_{\text{rel}}^2=\dfrac12\times\dfrac{15\times25}{40}\times40^2=7500$ J.
Heat capacity $=40\times31\times4.2=5208$ J/$^\circ$C.
$\Delta T=\dfrac{7500}{5208}\approx1.44\ ^\circ$C.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
In a screw gauge, the zero of the circular scale lies 3 divisions above the horizontal pitch line when their metallic studs are brought in contact. Using this instrument thickness of a sheet is measured. If pitch scale reading is 1 mm and the circular scale reading is 51 then the correct thickness of the sheet is __________ mm.
[Assume least count is 0.01 mm]
questions.sol:
Zero of the circular scale above the line means a negative zero error: $-3\times0.01=-0.03$ mm.
Observed reading $=1+51\times0.01=1.51$ mm.
Correct reading $=1.51-(-0.03)=1.54$ mm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A simple pendulum of string length 30 cm performs 20 oscillations in 10 s. The length of the string required for the pendulum to perform 40 oscillations in the same time duration is __________ cm. [Assume that the mass of the pendulum remains same.]
questions.sol:
The period must halve (from 0.5 s to 0.25 s).
$T\propto\sqrt l$, so the length becomes a quarter: $\dfrac{30}{4}=7.5$ cm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A 20 m long uniform copper wire held horizontally is allowed to fall under the gravity $(g=10\text{ m/s}^2)$ through a uniform horizontal magnetic field of 0.5 Gauss perpendicular to the length of the wire. The induced EMF across the wire when it travells a vertical distance of 200 m is __________ mV.
questions.sol:
Speed after falling 200 m: $v=\sqrt{2\times10\times200}=20\sqrt{10}$ m/s.
$\varepsilon=Blv=0.5\times10^{-4}\times20\times20\sqrt{10}=0.02\sqrt{10}$ V $=20\sqrt{10}$ mV.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Consider a ferromagnetic material :
Assertion (A) : The individual atoms in a ferromagnetic material possess a magnetic dipole moment and interact with one another in such a way that they spontaneously align themselves forming domains.
Reason (R) : At high enough temperature, the domain structure of ferromagnetic material disintegrates. Thus, magnetization will disappear at high enough temperature known as Curie temperature.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.sol:
(A) correctly describes how domains form in a ferromagnet: true.
(R) correctly describes the loss of ferromagnetism above the Curie temperature: true.
But (R) is about what happens on heating; it does not explain why domains form. So both are true and (R) is not the explanation of (A).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Match List - I with List - II.
List - I
Relation		List - II
Law
A. $\displaystyle\oint\vec E\cdot\vec{dl}=-\frac{d}{dt}\oint\vec B\cdot\vec{da}$I. Ampere's circuital law
B. $\displaystyle\oint\vec B\cdot\vec{dl}=\mu_0\left(I+\epsilon_0\frac{d\phi_E}{dt}\right)$II. Faraday's laws of electromagnetic induction
C. $\displaystyle\oint\vec E\cdot\vec{da}=\frac1{\epsilon_0}\int_v\rho\,dv$III. Ampere - Maxwell law
D. $\displaystyle\oint\vec B\cdot\vec{dl}=\mu_0I$IV. Gauss's law of electrostatics
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
A: induced EMF equals minus the rate of change of magnetic flux: Faraday (II).
B: conduction plus displacement current: Ampere-Maxwell (III).
C: electric flux through a closed surface equals enclosed charge over $\epsilon_0$: Gauss (IV).
D: Ampere's circuital law (I).
A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two point charges $2q$ and $q$ are placed at vertex $A$ and centre of face $CDEF$ of the cube as shown in figure. The electric flux passing through the cube is :
questions.sol:
A charge at a corner is shared by 8 such cubes, so this cube gets $\dfrac{2q}{8}=\dfrac q4$ of enclosed charge.
A charge at the centre of a face is shared by 2 cubes: $\dfrac q2$.
Flux $=\dfrac{1}{\epsilon_0}\left(\dfrac q4+\dfrac q2\right)=\dfrac{3q}{4\epsilon_0}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A wire of uniform resistance $\lambda\ \Omega$/m is bent into a circle of radius $r$ and another piece of wire with length $2r$ is connected between points $A$ and $B$ (AOB) as shown in figure. The equivalent resistance between points $A$ and $B$ is __________ $\Omega$.
questions.sol:
A and B are a quarter circle apart. Three paths join them in parallel: the minor arc $\dfrac{\pi r\lambda}{2}$, the major arc $\dfrac{3\pi r\lambda}{2}$ and the wire AOB, $2r\lambda$.
$\dfrac1{R_{eq}}=\dfrac1{r\lambda}\left(\dfrac2\pi+\dfrac2{3\pi}+\dfrac12\right)=\dfrac{16+3\pi}{6\pi r\lambda}$.
$R_{eq}=\dfrac{6\pi\lambda r}{3\pi+16}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A thin prism with angle $5^\circ$ of refractive index 1.72 is combined with another prism of refractive index 1.9 to produce dispersion without deviation. The angle of second prism is __________.
questions.sol:
No net deviation: $(\mu_1-1)A_1=(\mu_2-1)A_2$.
$0.72\times5^\circ=0.9\times A_2 \Rightarrow A_2=4^\circ$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Consider light travelling from a medium $A$ to medium $B$ separated by a plane interface. If the light undergoes total internal reflection during its travel from medium $A$ to $B$ and the speed of light in media $A$ and $B$ are $2.4\times10^8$ m/s and $2.7\times10^8$ m/s, respectively, then the value of critical angle is :
questions.sol:
$\sin C=\dfrac{n_B}{n_A}=\dfrac{v_A}{v_B}=\dfrac{2.4}{2.7}=\dfrac89$.
Then $\cos C=\dfrac{\sqrt{17}}{9}$ and $\tan C=\dfrac{8}{\sqrt{17}}$.
$C=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac8{\sqrt{17}}\right)$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The de Broglie wavelength of an oxygen molecule at $27^\circ$C is $x\times10^{-12}$ m. The value of $x$ is (take Planck's constant $=6.63\times10^{-34}$ J.s, Boltzmann constant $=1.38\times10^{-23}$ J/K, mass of oxygen molecule $=5.31\times10^{-26}$ kg)
questions.sol:
Using the rms speed, $p=\sqrt{3mkT}=\sqrt{3\times5.31\times10^{-26}\times1.38\times10^{-23}\times300}\approx2.57\times10^{-23}$ kg m/s.
$\lambda=\dfrac hp=\dfrac{6.63\times10^{-34}}{2.57\times10^{-23}}\approx2.6\times10^{-11}$ m $=26\times10^{-12}$ m.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text:
In hydrogen atom spectrum, $(R\rightarrow$ Rydberg's constant$)$
A. the maximum wavelength of the radiation of Lyman series is $\dfrac{4}{3R}$
B. the Balmer series lies in the visible region of the spectrum
C. the minimum wavelength of the radiation of Paschen series is $\dfrac9R$
D. the minimum wavelength of Lyman series is $\dfrac{5}{4R}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
A: Lyman longest line, $n=2\to1$: $\dfrac1\lambda=R\left(1-\dfrac14\right)$, $\lambda=\dfrac4{3R}$: true.
B: the Balmer lines are in the visible region: true.
C: Paschen shortest line, $\infty\to3$: $\lambda=\dfrac9R$: true.
D: Lyman shortest line, $\infty\to1$: $\lambda=\dfrac1R$, not $\dfrac5{4R}$: false.
A, B and C only.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The following diagram shows a Zener diode as a voltage regulator. The Zener diode is rated at $V_z=5$ V and the desired current in load is 5 mA. The unregulated voltage source can supply upto 25 V. Considering the Zener diode can withstand four times of the load current, the value of resistor $R_s$ (shown in circuit) should be __________$\Omega$.
questions.note: Dropped in the official final key: full marks to everyone. The working gives 800 Ω, which is not one of the options.
questions.sol:
Largest Zener current $=4\times5=20$ mA, so the current through $R_s$ at 25 V must not exceed $20+5=25$ mA.
$R_s=\dfrac{25-5}{25\times10^{-3}}=800\ \Omega$.
800 $\Omega$ is not among the options.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Using a variable frequency a.c. voltage source the maximum current measured in the given $LCR$ circuit is 50 mA for $V=5\sin(100t)$ The values of $L$ and $R$ are shown in the figure. The capacitance of the capacitor (C) used is __________ $\mu$F.
questions.sol:
The current is largest at resonance, where $I_0=\dfrac{V_0}{R}=\dfrac{5}{100}=50$ mA, as measured.
So $\omega=100$ rad/s is the resonant frequency: $\omega^2=\dfrac1{LC}$.
$C=\dfrac{1}{(100)^2\times2}=5\times10^{-5}$ F $=50\ \mu$F.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: In two separate Young's double-slit experimental set-ups and two monochromatic light sources of different wavelengths are used to get fringes of equal width. The ratios of the slits separations and that of the wavelengths of light used are $2:1$ and $1:2$ respectively. The corresponding ratio of the distances between the slits and the respective screens $(D_1/D_2)$ is __________.
questions.sol:
Fringe width $\beta=\dfrac{\lambda D}{d}$ is the same in both, so $D\propto\dfrac{d}{\lambda}$.
$\dfrac{D_1}{D_2}=\dfrac{d_1}{d_2}\cdot\dfrac{\lambda_2}{\lambda_1}=2\times2=4$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
The equation of the electric field of an electromagnetic wave propagating through free space is given by : $E=\sqrt{377}\sin\left(6.27\times10^3t-2.09\times10^{-5}x\right)$ N/C
The average power of the electromagnetic wave is $\left(\dfrac1\alpha\right)$ W/m$^2$. The value of $\alpha$ is __________
$\left(\text{Take }\sqrt{\dfrac{\mu_0}{\varepsilon_0}}=377\text{ in SI units}\right)$
questions.sol:
Average intensity $I=\dfrac12c\varepsilon_0E_0^2=\dfrac{E_0^2}{2\sqrt{\mu_0/\varepsilon_0}}$.
$I=\dfrac{377}{2\times377}=\dfrac12$ W/m$^2$, so $\alpha=2$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A simple pendulum made of mass 10 g and a metallic wire of length 10 cm is suspended vertically in a uniform magnetic field of 2 T. The magnetic field direction is perpendicular to the plane of oscillations of the pendulum. If the pendulum is released from an angle of $60^\circ$ with vertical, then maximum induced EMF between the point of suspension and point of oscillation is __________ mV. (Take $g=10$ m/s$^2$)
questions.sol:
Greatest speed at the lowest point: $v=\sqrt{2gl(1-\cos60^\circ)}=\sqrt{2\times10\times0.1\times0.5}=1$ m/s, so $\omega=\dfrac vl=10$ rad/s.
EMF across a rod rotating about one end: $\varepsilon=\dfrac12B\omega l^2=\dfrac12\times2\times10\times(0.1)^2=0.1$ V $=100$ mV.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The space between the plates of a parallel plate capacitor of capacitance C (without any dielectric) is now filled with three dielectric slabs of dielectric constants $K_1=2$, $K_2=3$ and $K_3=5$ (as shown in figure). If new capacitance is $\dfrac n3C$ then the value of $n$ is __________.
questions.sol:
Upper half: $K_1$ across the full area, thickness $\dfrac d2$: $C_1=2K_1C=4C$.
Lower half: $K_2$ and $K_3$ side by side, each area $\dfrac A2$, thickness $\dfrac d2$: $C_2=(K_2+K_3)C=8C$.
In series: $\dfrac{4C\times8C}{12C}=\dfrac83C$, so $n=8$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding the energy of the stationary state is true in the following one - electron systems ?
options: $-1.09\times10^{-18}$ J for second orbit of H atom.
$+2.18\times10^{-18}$ J for second orbit of $\mathrm{He^+}$ ion
$+8.72\times10^{-18}$ J for first orbit of $\mathrm{He^+}$ ion
$-2.18\times10^{-18}$ J for third orbit of $\mathrm{Li^{2+}}$ ion
questions.sol:
$E_n=-2.18\times10^{-18}\dfrac{Z^2}{n^2}$ J, always negative.
H, $n=2$: $-5.45\times10^{-19}$ J. $\mathrm{He^+}$, $n=2$: $-2.18\times10^{-18}$ J; $n=1$: $-8.72\times10^{-18}$ J (both options have the wrong sign).
$\mathrm{Li^{2+}}$, $n=3$: $-2.18\times10^{-18}\times\dfrac99=-2.18\times10^{-18}$ J: true.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given,
(A) $n=5$, $m_l=-1$
(B) $n=3$, $l=2$, $m_l=-1$, $m_s=+\dfrac12$
The maximum number of electron(s) in an atom that can have the quantum numbers as given in (A) and (B) respectively are :
questions.sol:
(A) For $n=5$, $m_l=-1$ is possible for $l=1,2,3,4$: 4 orbitals, 8 electrons.
(B) All four quantum numbers are fixed: 1 electron.
8 and 1.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Identify the molecule (X) with maximum number of lone pairs of electrons (obtained using Lewis dot structure) among $\mathrm{HNO_3}$, $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$, $\mathrm{NF_3}$ and $\mathrm{O_3}$. Choose the correct bond angle made by the central atom of the molecule (X).
questions.sol:
Lone pairs: $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ 7 (2 + 2 + 3 on the oxygens); $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ 8 (2 on each O); $\mathrm{NF_3}$ 10 (3 on each F + 1 on N); $\mathrm{O_3}$ 6.
X is $\mathrm{NF_3}$, a pyramidal molecule with F-N-F angle about $102^\circ$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: A cup of water at 5$^\circ$C (system) is placed in a microwave oven and the oven is turned on for one minute during which the water begins to boil. Which of the following option is true ?
questions.sol:
The water absorbs energy and its temperature rises: q is positive.
As it heats and starts to boil it expands against the atmosphere, so work is done by the system: w is negative (small).
The internal energy increases: $\Delta U$ is positive.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Which one of the following graphs accurately represents the plot of partial pressure of $\mathrm{CS_2}$ vs its mole fraction in a mixture of acetone and $\mathrm{CS_2}$ at constant temperature ?
questions.sol:
Acetone and $\mathrm{CS_2}$ show positive deviation from Raoult's law.
So the partial pressure of $\mathrm{CS_2}$ lies above the Raoult's law line, follows Henry's law (a steeper straight line) at low $x_{\mathrm{CS_2}}$ and meets $p^\circ_{\mathrm{CS_2}}$ at $x=1$.
That is graph (1).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the general reaction given below at 400 K
$x\mathrm{A(g)}\rightleftharpoons y\mathrm{B(g)}$.
The values of $K_p$ and $K_c$ are studied under the same condition of temperature but variation in $x$ and $y$.
(i) $K_p=85.87$ and $K_c=2.586$ appropriate units
(ii) $K_p=0.862$ and $K_c=28.62$ appropriate units
The values of $x$ and $y$ in (i) and (ii) respectively are :
questions.sol:
$K_p=K_c(RT)^{\Delta n}$ with $RT=0.0821\times400\approx32.8$.
(i) $\dfrac{K_p}{K_c}=\dfrac{85.87}{2.586}\approx33.2$, so $\Delta n=y-x=1$: $x=1$, $y=2$.
(ii) $\dfrac{K_p}{K_c}=\dfrac{0.862}{28.62}\approx\dfrac1{33.2}$, so $\Delta n=-1$: $x=2$, $y=1$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
In the given electrochemical cell, $\mathrm{Ag(s)\,|\,AgCl(s)\,|\,FeCl_2(aq), FeCl_3(aq)\,|\,Pt(s)}$ at 298 K, the cell potential $\left(E_{\text{cell}}\right)$ will increase when :
A. Concentration of $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ is increased.
B. Concentration of $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ is decreased.
C. Concentration of $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ is decreased.
D. Concentration of $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ is increased.
E. Concentration of $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ is increased.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Cell reaction: $\mathrm{Ag+Cl^-+Fe^{3+}\rightarrow AgCl+Fe^{2+}}$.
$E_{\text{cell}}=E^\circ_{\text{cell}}-0.059\log\dfrac{[\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}]}{[\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}][\mathrm{Cl^-}]}$.
$E_{\text{cell}}$ rises when $[\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}]$ falls or $[\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}]$ or $[\mathrm{Cl^-}]$ rises: C, D and E.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The correct trend in the first ionization enthalpies of the elements in the 3$^{\text{rd}}$ period of periodic table is :
questions.sol:
Ionisation enthalpy generally rises across period 3: Al (577), Si (786), P (1012), S (1000), Cl (1251) kJ/mol.
P is higher than S because its half-filled 3p subshell is extra stable.
Order: Al $<$ Si $<$ S $<$ P $<$ Cl.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text:
The correct statements from the following are :
A. Ionic radii of trivalent cations of group 13 elements decreases down the group.
B. Electronegativity of group 13 elements decreases down the group.
C. Among the group 13 elements, Boron has highest first ionisation enthalpy.
D. The trichloride and triiodide of group 13 elements are covalent in nature.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
A: ionic radii of $\mathrm{M^{3+}}$ increase down the group: false.
B: electronegativity falls from B to Al and then rises slightly (Ga, In, Tl), so it does not decrease down the group: false.
C: boron, the smallest atom, has the highest first ionisation enthalpy: true.
D: the trichlorides and triiodides are covalent: true.
C and D only.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I :
$\mathrm{[CoBr_4]^{2-}}$ ion will absorb light of lower energy than $\mathrm{[CoCl_4]^{2-}}$ ion.
Statement II :
In $\mathrm{[CoI_4]^{2-}}$ ion, the energy separation between the two set of d-orbitals is more than $\mathrm{[CoCl_4]^{2-}}$ ion.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Spectrochemical series: $\mathrm{I^-<Br^-<Cl^-}$.
$\mathrm{Br^-}$ gives a smaller splitting than $\mathrm{Cl^-}$, so $\mathrm{[CoBr_4]^{2-}}$ absorbs lower-energy light: Statement I is true.
$\mathrm{I^-}$ gives an even smaller splitting than $\mathrm{Cl^-}$: Statement II is false.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The statements that are incorrect about the nickel(II) complex of dimethylglyoxime are :
A. It is red in colour.
B. It has a high solubility in water at pH $=$ 9.
C. The Ni ion has two unpaired d-electrons.
D. The N $-$ Ni $-$ N bond angle is almost close to $90^\circ$.
E. The complex contains four five-membered metallacycles (metal containing rings).
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{[Ni(dmg)_2]}$ is a red precipitate (A correct) that is insoluble in water, even in ammoniacal (pH about 9) solution (B incorrect).
It is square planar ($\mathrm{dsp^2}$) with $\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}$ $\mathrm{d^8}$ spin-paired, so no unpaired electrons (C incorrect); N-Ni-N angles are about $90^\circ$ (D correct).
It has two five-membered chelate rings (the other two rings are six-membered, closed by hydrogen bonds), so E is incorrect.
Incorrect: B, C and E.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Match List - I with List - II.
List - I
Functional group (detection)		List - II
Change observed during detection
A. Unsaturation (Baeyer's test)I. Red colour appears
B. Alcoholic group (Ceric ammonium nitrate test)II. Silver mirror appears
C. Aldehyde group (Tollen's reagent)III. Violet colour appears
D. Phenolic group ($\mathrm{FeCl_3}$ test)IV. Discharge of pink colour
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
A: alkaline $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ loses its pink colour (IV).
B: ceric ammonium nitrate turns red with an alcohol (I).
C: Tollens' reagent gives a silver mirror (II).
D: neutral $\mathrm{FeCl_3}$ gives a violet colour with phenol (III).
A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I :
Sublimation is used for the separation and purification of compounds with low melting point.
Statement II :
The boiling point of a liquid increases as the external pressure is reduced.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Sublimation purifies compounds that pass directly from solid to vapour (sublimable compounds), not compounds simply because they have a low melting point: Statement I is false.
A liquid boils when its vapour pressure equals the external pressure, so lowering the pressure lowers the boiling point (the basis of distillation under reduced pressure): Statement II is false.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text:
Consider the following compounds
Arrange these compounds in the increasing order of reactivity with nitrating mixture.
questions.sol:
Nitration is electrophilic substitution, so electron-donating groups speed it up and electron-withdrawing groups slow it down.
$\mathrm{-OCH_3}$ (c) strongly activates; $\mathrm{-Cl}$ (a) mildly deactivates; $\mathrm{-NO_2}$ (b) strongly deactivates.
Order: b $<$ a $<$ c.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
But-2-yne and hydrogen (one mole each) are separately treated with (i) Pd/C and (ii) Na/liq. $\mathrm{NH_3}$ to give the products X and Y respectively.
Identify the incorrect statements.
A. X and Y are stereoisomers.
B. Dipole moment of X is zero.
C. Boiling point of X is higher than Y.
D. X and Y react with $\mathrm{O_3/Zn+H_2O}$ to give different products.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Catalytic (Pd) addition of one mole of $\mathrm{H_2}$ is syn: X is cis-but-2-ene. Na/liq. $\mathrm{NH_3}$ gives Y, trans-but-2-ene.
A: they are geometrical isomers: correct. B: cis-but-2-ene has a small dipole moment, not zero: incorrect.
C: the polar cis isomer boils higher: correct. D: both give two molecules of ethanal on ozonolysis: incorrect.
Incorrect statements: B and D.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The correct sequence of reagents for the above conversion of X to Y is :
questions.sol:
X is 1-bromo-1-phenylethane and Y is phenylethanoic acid, with the COOH on the end carbon.
NaOEt eliminates HBr to give styrene, $\mathrm{C_6H_5CH=CH_2}$.
Hydroboration-oxidation adds water anti-Markovnikov: $\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2CH_2OH}$.
Jones reagent oxidises the primary alcohol to $\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2COOH}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: '$x$' is the product which is obtained from propanenitrile and stannous chloride in the presence of hydrochloric acid followed by hydrolysis. '$y$' is the product which is obtained from the but-2-ene by the ozonolysis followed by hydrolysis. From the following, which product is not obtained when one mole of '$x$' and one mole of '$y$' react with each other in the presence of alkali followed by heating ?
questions.sol:
Stephen reduction: $x$ is propanal, $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CHO}$. Ozonolysis of but-2-ene: $y$ is ethanal, $\mathrm{CH_3CHO}$.
Crossed aldol condensation gives four products: ethanal + ethanal: but-2-enal; propanal + propanal: 2-methylpent-2-enal; propanal (as enolate) + ethanal: 2-methylbut-2-enal; ethanal (as enolate) + propanal: pent-2-enal.
3-Methylbut-2-enal is not formed.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Compound 'P' undergoes the following sequence of reactions :
'P' is :
questions.sol:
The final product, cyclohexyl isocyanide, comes from cyclohexylamine by the carbylamine reaction ($\mathrm{CHCl_3}$, alcoholic KOH).
Cyclohexylamine comes from cyclohexanecarboxamide (Q) by Hofmann bromamide degradation ($\mathrm{Br_2}$, KOH), which removes one carbon.
The amide comes from the acid with $\mathrm{NH_3}$ and heat, so P is cyclohexanecarboxylic acid, structure (1).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the following sequence of reactions.
Assuming that the reaction proceeds to completion, then 137 mg of 4-nitrotoluene will produce __________ mg of B.
(Given molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ H : 1, C : 12, N : 14, O : 16, Br : 80)
questions.sol:
4-Nitrotoluene ($M=137$) is reduced to 4-methylaniline (A), acetylated to N-(4-methylphenyl)ethanamide, and brominated ortho to the NHCOCH$_3$ group.
B is 2-bromo-4-methylacetanilide, $\mathrm{C_9H_{10}BrNO}$, $M=108+10+80+14+16=228$.
137 mg is 1 mmol, giving 1 mmol of B $=228$ mg.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: From the given following (A to D) cyclic structures, those which will not react with Tollen's reagent are :
questions.sol:
A and D have a free OH on the anomeric carbon (hemiacetals), so they open to the aldehyde form and reduce Tollens' reagent.
B and C have $\mathrm{OCH_3}$ on the anomeric carbon (glycosides, acetals); the ring cannot open, so they do not react.
Answer: B and C.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
$x$ mg of pure HCl was used to make an aqueous solution. 25.0 mL of 0.1 M $\mathrm{Ba(OH)_2}$ solution is used when the HCl solution was titrated against it. The numerical value of $x$ is __________ $\times10^{-1}$. (Nearest integer)
Given : Molar mass of HCl and $\mathrm{Ba(OH)_2}$ are 36.5 and 171.0 g mol$^{-1}$ respectively.
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{Ba(OH)_2}$: $25.0\times0.1=2.5$ mmol, which neutralises $2\times2.5=5$ mmol HCl.
Mass of HCl $=5\times36.5=182.5$ mg $=1825\times10^{-1}$ mg.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
For the following gas phase equilibrium reaction at constant temperature,
$\mathrm{NH_3(g)\rightleftharpoons\frac12N_2(g)+\frac32H_2(g)}$
if the total pressure is $\sqrt3$ atm and the pressure equilibrium constant $\left(K_p\right)$ is 9 atm, then the degree of dissociation is given as $\left(x\times10^{-2}\right)^{-1/2}$. The value of $x$ is __________. (nearest integer)
questions.sol:
Start with 1 mol $\mathrm{NH_3}$: at equilibrium $1-\alpha$, $\dfrac\alpha2$, $\dfrac{3\alpha}2$; total $1+\alpha$.
$K_p=\dfrac{\left(\frac\alpha2\right)^{1/2}\left(\frac{3\alpha}2\right)^{3/2}}{1-\alpha}\cdot\dfrac{P}{1+\alpha}=\dfrac{3\sqrt3\,\alpha^2P}{4(1-\alpha^2)}$.
With $P=\sqrt3$: $\dfrac{9\alpha^2}{4(1-\alpha^2)}=9 \Rightarrow \alpha^2=\dfrac45$.
$\alpha=\left(\dfrac54\right)^{-1/2}=\left(125\times10^{-2}\right)^{-1/2}$, so $x=125$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
For the thermal decomposition of reactant AB(g), the following plot is constructed.
The half life of the reaction is '$x$' min.
$x=$ __________ min. (Nearest integer)
questions.sol:
[AB] falls linearly with time, so the reaction is zero order.
Slope: $k=\dfrac{0.55-0.50}{100}=5\times10^{-4}$ M s$^{-1}$, and $[AB]_0=0.6$ M.
$t_{1/2}=\dfrac{[AB]_0}{2k}=\dfrac{0.6}{2\times5\times10^{-4}}=600$ s $=10$ min.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The crystal field splitting energy of $\mathrm{[Co(oxalate)_3]^{3-}}$ complex is 'n' times that of the $\mathrm{[Cr(oxalate)_3]^{3-}}$ complex. Here 'n' is __________. (Assume $\Delta_o>>P$)
questions.sol:
Read as crystal field stabilisation energy, with the same $\Delta_o$ for both oxalate complexes.
$\mathrm{Co^{3+}}$, $\mathrm{d^6}$, low spin ($\Delta_o\gg P$): $t_{2g}^6$, CFSE $=-2.4\Delta_o$.
$\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}$, $\mathrm{d^3}$: $t_{2g}^3$, CFSE $=-1.2\Delta_o$.
$n=\dfrac{2.4}{1.2}=2$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Consider all the structural isomers with molecular formula $\mathrm{C_5H_{11}Br}$ are separately treated with KOH(aq) to give respective substitution products, without any rearrangement. The number of products which can exhibit optical isomerism from these is __________.
questions.note: Official final key: 3 or 6 (either answer is awarded marks). 3 counts the chiral alcohols by structure; 6 counts each of their two enantiomers.
questions.sol:
The 8 structural isomers of $\mathrm{C_5H_{11}Br}$ give the 8 alcohols $\mathrm{C_5H_{11}OH}$ with the same skeletons.
Chiral ones: pentan-2-ol, 2-methylbutan-1-ol and 3-methylbutan-2-ol. (Pentan-1-ol, pentan-3-ol, 3-methylbutan-1-ol, 2-methylbutan-2-ol and 2,2-dimethylpropan-1-ol are not chiral.)
Answer: 3.
questions.subject: Chemistry
